items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: Otto was the lead saxophone, I was second alto, Crawford was the third alto and Bingie -- three altos and one tenor. We played four-part harmony to everything without music, and we broadcast without music.

ctx.x: But that was his fun. He'd give each waiter a $100.00 -- each singer a $100.00 bill and make her stick that in her stocking. And we'd have to keep an eye on the entertainers because they'd go south with the money -- they had to come back and put in the box, you know -- we'd split it up. And we -- instead of playing the music for the entertainers we always had a lookout. My turn to look out. You just pretend you're playing, but you watch every move.
